analysis: What changed since the 7:00 AM PT brief: the tape has cooled since the open but not recovered — IBD's read just after the open has the Dow down ~600 points (-1.1%) with the Nasdaq roughly flat, versus Investopedia's early snapshot of Dow -1%, S&P -0.6%, Nasdaq -0.3%. Either way, the same rotation: energy and defensives bid, AI-crowded names sold, with the 10Y back to 4.98% (+3bps) after its worst one-day drop since March 2023 and Brent at $115.40 on the WSJ-carried Iran threat. The two stabilizing tells are strengthening modestly: the memory bounce is holding (DRAM +3.5%, SK Hynix +3.5%, SOXX +1%) and SpaceX has flipped green (+1%) after Thursday's 9% tank while CCI (+12%) and AMT (+6-8%) keep pricing the 80,000-cell-site plan — still single-source, still fragile. The counterweight got harsher: Comfort Systems joined the 'beat and still sell' club (-12% on a 69% profit surge with raised dividend), and Meta's defense wall keeps cracking — KeyCorp $905 and DA Davidson bullishness sit next to Piper Sandler's raised opex/capex estimates and Mizuho's warning of a potential equity raise in early 2027, with ARK buying the dip (38,110 shares) for the retail-sentiment counter. Megacap live quotes are mixed-steady (MSFT +0.8%, NVDA +0.4%, TSLA -0.3%, AAPL flat per Finnhub), a far cry from Thursday's uniform red. Signal vs noise: crude and the 10Y are confirmed macro signal; the memory/SpaceX rebounds are early but holding; Mizuho's equity-raise warning is one-firm, conditional analysis, not a filing — treat as opinion, not fact. The day is still the same crowded-AI deleveraging into the FOMC blackout.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Dow down ~600 points (-1.1%) just after the open, S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq roughly flat in early trading (IBD live coverage); Investopedia's early snapshot had Dow -1% (-550 pts), S&P 500 -0.6%, Nasdaq -0.3%. Entering today the Dow was up 1.7% on the week — still on pace for a third straight weekly gain — while the S&P 500 was +0.1% and the Nasdaq -0.5% for the week.
headlines.why_it_matters: Flat Nasdaq against a down Dow is rotation, not panic — money keeps moving from crowded AI into energy and defensives rather than leaving equities.

headlines.headline: WTI crude +~3% to ~$102.35 and Brent +2% to $115.40, the highest since early May (IBD; Investopedia), as Iran warned that renewed U.S.-Israel strikes would trigger retaliation against airports, oil pipelines and other Persian Gulf infrastructure (WSJ). The 10Y Treasury yield edged up 3bps to 4.98% after suffering its worst one-day drop since March 2023 on Thursday.
headlines.why_it_matters: $100+ crude plus a near-5% 10Y is the stagflation shadow over every rally attempt — today's energy strength is a hedge bid, not a growth signal; Thursday's 17bp bond rally already reversed.

headlines.headline: Meta slips another ~1% early Friday after Thursday's 7% slide ($648.85 close). Analysts keep raising targets — KeyCorp $905 (overweight), DA Davidson positive, Barclays $880, Goldman $860, UBS $892 — but the stock keeps getting sold. Piper Sandler raised 2027 opex/capex estimates; Mizuho warned shares could struggle ahead of a potential equity raise in early 2027 (single firm opinion, not confirmed). ARK bought 38,110 shares across three ETFs on the dip; retail sentiment stays bullish (Stocktwits). Earnings context: Q3 revenue $64.6B (+26%, beat $63.4B est), EPS $3.83 (vs $6.52 ex the teen mental health settlement charge per Zacks), first quarterly FCF outflow (-$2.12B vs +$10.63B a year ago), 2026 capex guide $135-145B, new Class C nonvoting shares slated for late Jan 2027 trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: Revenue and EPS beats no longer matter when the funding question dominates — record-high target hikes failing to lift the tape is the cleanest sentiment read on AI capex, and the first FCF outflow in history is the fact everyone is trading.

headlines.headline: Memory and AI-tied names bounce early and hold: the DRAM Memory ETF +3.5% after Thursday's 7% plunge, SK Hynix +3.5% (Solidigm U.S. IPO plans scrapped), and SOXX +1% after a ~6.5% drop. Live megacap quotes (Finnhub, ~8am PT): MSFT +0.8% ($525.29), NVDA +0.4% ($213.11), TSLA -0.3% ($373.59), AAPL flat ($348.22). Thursday's damage for reference: META -7%, AMZN -4.6%, NVDA -4.4%, TSLA -3.1%, GOOGL -3.1%, MSFT -2.2%, AAPL +1.2% (Summa Money).
headlines.why_it_matters: The deepest-sold AI-adjacent names leading the bounce is the classic early-stabilization tell — mixed-steady megacap quotes beat Thursday's uniform red, but 'beat and still sell' discipline is alive, so the bounce needs to hold into the close.

headlines.headline: SpaceX flips +1% early after tanking 9% Thursday on the Bloomberg report that it is targeting 80,000+ U.S. cell sites for a fourth nationwide wireless network, in talks with cell infrastructure firms (IBD; Investopedia). Towers keep soaring — Crown Castle +12%, American Tower +6-8% — while carriers stay under pressure: T, VZ, TMUS down 2.5-4% (TMUS -3.5%). SpaceX has not commented; TD Cowen estimates a terrestrial build would cost $80B+. Multiple outlets carry the Bloomberg story, but the underlying plan still rests on unnamed sources — single-source, unconfirmed, treat as fragile.
headlines.why_it_matters: The short-carriers/long-towers pair trade keeps working — but both legs snap at once if the report gets confirmed or denied; SpaceX's rebound prices the optionality, not a confirmed plan.

headlines.headline: Post-earnings fades dominate: Bloom Energy -12% despite a big beat (94c EPS vs ~69c est, revenue $1.24B +138% vs $1.07B est, raised FY guidance — IBD); Comfort Systems -12% despite a 69% profit surge and raised dividend; Western Digital -3% after its beat-and-raise (EPS $4.64 vs $4.11 est, revenue $4.38B +55%); American Express -3.5%; Deckers (Ugg/Hoka) -6 to -9%; Moderna down another 7% after Thursday's -18% worst-in-S&P-500 drop on an apparent cancer-vaccine data leak. MaxLinear the exception: +5% on its beat and guidance.
headlines.why_it_matters: 'Beat and still sell' is the session's discipline — results have to clear a higher bar than consensus when AI-capex funding is the question; only guided-higher MaxLinear is being rewarded.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried: Q3 cash distribution $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) payable Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26 — the record date is Monday; Q3 earnings before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 AM ET call.
